references.text: The commandment for a holy convocation and the prohibition of work on the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread is also given in connection with the institution of Passover in Egypt.
The Sabbath command prohibiting work, a fundamental principle that also applies to the festival days with holy convocations.
The holy convocation and work prohibition of the Sabbath, which serve as a pattern for the other festival days mentioned in the same chapter.
The seventh day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread has the same provision for a holy convocation and prohibition of work.
The Feast of Weeks (Pentecost) has the same commandment for a holy convocation and prohibition of work.
The Feast of Tabernacles has similar provisions for a holy convocation and prohibition of work on the first and eighth days.
A parallel text in Numbers that repeats the commandment for a holy convocation and prohibition of work on the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
Deuteronomy's provision regarding the seventh day as a festival assembly with a prohibition of work.
The Epistle to the Hebrews speaks of a Sabbath rest that remains for God's people, linking the days of rest to the final rest in Christ.
Paul explains that the festivals, new moon days, and Sabbaths were a shadow of what was to come, but the reality is Christ.
